reason: Refuted as a command-cut remedy, not as evidence that the helpers enforce the promise. The exact cited line exists at commands/autonomous-run.md:62 and is outside every shared block, verified against the exact lengths and contents of its commands/_shared sources. governor.sh is a synchronous once-per-attempt check (lines 9-10, 32-64); launch-background-run.sh:161-172 starts nohup and exits without an independently running timeout or feed writer. However, the proposed replacement with manual intervention would remove a behavior explicitly required by evals/scenarios/92-background-autonomous-run.md:9,16,34 and by accepted ADR-0081 decision 1 at line 17. ADR-0081 also rejects a bespoke daemon controller in Alternatives considered. STOP ON ADR: neither weakening the guarantee nor selecting an independent supervisor is an authorized editorial correction; application requires a policy decision. Independent recursive directory grep over commands for governor.s wall-clock timeout|stalls until|stall-to-escalation finds only autonomous-run.md:62. The live doctrine repeats it at wos/autonomous-track.md:97; the recorded policy and scenario are the additional contract sites. Recursive scripts searches and the complete launcher/governor reads found no timeout supervisor wired to this launcher. No source change or runtime test was performed.
corrected_claim: There is a real implementation-to-contract gap: the shipped launcher and synchronous governor do not enforce ADR-0081's promised automatic permission-stall timeout and escalation while the agent cannot return to the next governor call. Preserve this as an implementation/policy issue requiring an explicit decision; do not silently replace the recorded stall-to-escalation policy with manual intervention.

The cited frontmatter line at commands/design-bootstrap.md:3 is present and command-local, but this is not a criterion-3 violation. It explicitly says when to use the command and excludes two meaningful cases: existing design-system docs and absence of a Figma file. It names no nonexistent sibling. The locked rubric does not require a sibling recommendation for each negative trigger. inventory-snapshot is a real refresh command (its lines 36-40 require a workspace and Figma URL, and its operating rules refresh the inventory), but its existence does not make that continuation mandatory in design-bootstrap's description. ADR-0135 gates aggregate description size; its scope explicitly leaves routing measurement open and changes no descriptions. Adding a sibling here is an optional usability preference, not a checkable defect under the stated trigger test.
